idiom_name: free functions + one shared ops table per type (no stateless member)
implementation_notes: C has neither base classes nor standard zero-sized objects: a struct definition with no named members is not valid ISO C (cppreference describes the behavior as undefined for C11-C23), although GCC documents a size-0 empty-structure extension. A member of an ordinary empty-like marker cannot be used as a portable free field: it needs a complete type and contributes at least one byte plus any alignment padding. The language-appropriate replacement is therefore to keep stateless behavior out of the object entirely: express it as free functions taking the object pointer, or carry one shared per-type ops table (function pointers selected by a type tag) so per-instance storage holds only state. Hand-written prefix-struct layering remains justified when a stable ABI prefix is required, but it is a C ABI technique rather than EBO.
pitfalls: An empty struct is not valid ISO C (cppreference describes a definition without named members as undefined behavior through C23); GCC documents size 0 only as an extension, so never build a portable layout on it.
A 'stateless' member never becomes free: struct { char c; struct marker m; } can grow by a byte plus padding, and the compiler may reorder nothing to help.
The prefix-struct idiom for hand-rolled inheritance breaks the common initial sequence as soon as a level adds leading data or when the prefix is not the first member.
alternative: Keep stateless behaviour in free functions taking the object pointer, or in one shared per-type ops/vtable struct selected by a type tag; C has no base-class subobjects, so no object size is consumed by behaviour at all.
